# Importing data for study 

This section provides a detailed explanation of how to use `getDataForStudy` function. For a general overview, refer to the [Getting Started](a00_introduction.html#study-configuration) section. Regarding data sources, there are three options: providing existing data, running a saved study, or using the CDM as a data source. 


```{r, eval = FALSE, echo = TRUE}
getDataForStudy(cdm = cdm, studyEnv = studyEnv)
```


Every import needs the `studyEnv` returned by
`cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration()`. It supplies the study location, cohort
definitions and cleaning settings. For a fresh study, individual settings can be
overridden in the import call. A saved study restores its analytical settings.

<br>

## Use CDM

For a fresh study configured with `runSavedStudy = FALSE`, set `useCDM = TRUE`
to import the cohorts specified by `atlasStateCohorts` and `atlasTargetCohort`.
Pass the connected CDM object as `cdm`.

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
getDataForStudy(
  cdm = cdm,
  studyEnv = studyEnv,
  useCDM = TRUE
)
```

<br>

### Without atlas support 

To use the CDM without ATLAS support, ensure the required JSON files are located under `studyName/JSON`. In this case, set the `baseUrl` variable to `NULL`.

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
getDataForStudy(
  cdm = cdm,
  studyEnv = studyEnv,
  useCDM = TRUE,
  baseUrl = NULL
)
```

<br>

## Run saved study

Copy the completed study's `Settings` folder into the named study folder,
then configure it with `runSavedStudy = TRUE`. The RDS file contains both the
analysis settings and the cohort definitions used by that run. Import fresh data
from the new CDM using those saved definitions, without an ATLAS connection or
working JSON files. Do not repeat analytical arguments such as
state labels, transition rules or merging options in either call.

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
studyEnv <- cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration(
  studyName = "nameForStudy",
  pathToStudy = getwd(),
  runSavedStudy = TRUE
)
getDataForStudy(cdm = newCdm, studyEnv = studyEnv)
```

<br>

## Add data object or path to data 

For a fresh local-data study, configure `useCDM = FALSE` and
`runSavedStudy = FALSE`. Import the configured input with
`getDataForStudy(studyEnv = studyEnv)`, or choose one replacement input:

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
# Use a new data frame, even if a CSV path was configured.
getDataForStudy(studyEnv = studyEnv, trajectoryDataObject = rawData)

# Alternatively, use a CSV, even if a data frame was configured.
getDataForStudy(studyEnv = studyEnv, pathToData = "path/to/data/data.csv")
```

An explicitly supplied input takes precedence over the configured alternative.
Do not supply both a non-NULL `trajectoryDataObject` and a non-NULL `pathToData`
in the same call. With neither supplied, the configured input is used.
An import override does not replace the configured local source for later calls.

For appending personal data to existing datasets, refer to the [create trajectories](a03_trajectories.html#adding-personal-data-to-self-inserted-data) section.
